properties.statement:
THE EXPERIMENT PLANNED IN JULY 2026 (BL-83b) WAS FINALLY RUN, 2026-08-20, on Anthony's word. Option (b): on a copy, contracts harvested, NO requirements recovered.

SETUP, with every precondition the decision named honoured: a scratch store outside the project tree that MINTED ITS OWN `graph_id` (818eb25bd9c0f823) rather than being told one; all access through `tools/reflow2_cli.py --graph <probe>` so no MCP write tool could touch the live graph; scope DERIVED from `git ls-files` minus two named rules rather than hand-picked — which is how `schema/` (11 files) came into scope, the exact directory a hand-picked sweep missed for eleven releases.

RECOVERED: 153 nodes, 411 edges — 69 components, 14 interfaces, 91 CONSUMES.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 THE HEADLINE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE PREDICTION, AND IT IS THE USEFUL RESULT

The decision predicted "a RECOVERED CONTRACT SET reflow2's own graph does not have" and called it THE PRIZE. On raw counts it looked won — 91 CONSUMES against the real graph's 17, and 60 of 69 components on a boundary against 14 of 56.

**IT COLLAPSED ON INSPECTION.** Of 33 modules the scan said CONSUME `req-dyno-core-api`, the references are: `Value` ×76, `DynoError` ×18, `PropertySpec` ×1. **95 of 95 are TYPES. Not one call.** Separating behaviour from type-vocabulary across all five suppliers:

  dynograph_core        behaviour 0    types 47 modules
  dynograph_storage     behaviour 1 (graph — StorageEngine)   types 16
  dynograph_graph       behaviour 3 (allocate, flow, structure)
  dynograph_vector      behaviour 1 (dimensions)
  dynograph_resolution  behaviour 2 (ingest, seam)

⭐⭐ THOSE ARE EXACTLY THE EDGES REFLOW2'S GRAPH ALREADY HAD, redrawn by hand the day before from the same imports. **THE HAND-AUTHORED SPARSE SET WAS RIGHT AND THE MECHANICAL DENSE SET WAS WRONG.** Importing the 57 proposed edges would have added 33 to a supplier whose every reference is a type, made "what breaks if dyno-core changes?" answer "everything", and buried the five real dependencies in noise.

⇒ THE FINDING ABOUT ADOPT, which is what the decision said the run would MEASURE: **A MECHANICAL SCAN CANNOT DISTINGUISH IMPORTING A TYPE FROM CALLING BEHAVIOUR, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE CONTENT OF A CONTRACT.** Adopt's Phase 1 says "both sides of every contract — this is where the structural findings come from", and it is right that the findings are there; it is wrong that reading imports gets you contracts. It gets you coupling, which is a different thing.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
✅ WHAT IT DID FIND, AND IT WAS WORTH THE RUN: THREE CIRCULAR DEPENDENCIES

  mcp-service ↔ mcp-skills
  mcp-proxy ↔ mcp-shared
  core-artifact → core-temporal → core-verify → core-artifact

All three verified line by line and ALL THREE FIXED THE SAME DAY. **None was a bug.** A module cycle inside one crate is legal Rust and compiles silently forever — nothing in the build was ever going to mention them, and nothing had, for as long as shared mode has existed.

⚠️ AND THE FIRST PASS REPORTED A FOURTH THAT WAS NOT REAL. `core-graph ↔ core-hierarchy` came from a rustdoc link in a COMMENT — the exact trap the adopt skill warns about in as many words ("structure from imports and calls, never from prose"). Stripping comments removed 26 of 175 coupling edges, **15% of the model was prose**, and the correction did not merely delete a false finding: it REVEALED the real three-hop cycle the noise had masked.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 THREE FURTHER FACTS THE RUN ESTABLISHED

(1) **21 of 66 modules have NO Component in the live design**, including `cmp:seam`, which the CONSUMES repair had hit from the other direction the day before.
(2) **reflow2's source cannot be a BLIND adopt subject.** 207 files name design ids in their comments (`dec:ask-not-repair` alone appears 29 times). A code-only copy was made at /home/ajs7/project/reflow2-code-only with docs, skills and every top-level markdown stripped — and it is still not blind, because the intent is IN THE CODE. Deleting files cannot undo that.
(3) The predicted "NEAR-ZERO functional agreement" was not testable as stated: no capabilities were recovered, so `evaluate_allocation` returned `modularity: None` — which is the fix shipped the same day working correctly on an independent graph rather than manufacturing 1.00 over nothing.
